answer: Each epoch, every node must commit a unique Blake3 hash over a dedicated 32 GB RAM array before voting rights activate; the verifier then samples random offsets inside that array, demanding proofs within a 15-millisecond window. A hollow identity farm cannot fake this voyage, since renting 500 such arrays for the 6-hour epoch costs roughly $41000 in spot memory, while genuine agents amortize the same nectar across productive inference. First, the node seals its root; next, peers challenge; on failure, the stake is slashed and the seat revoked.
